angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 480,729 km at 196.64 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.0856 +/- 0.0186 mas (same row, RUWE 0.98): 196.64 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.691 +/- 0.053 solar radii from Christiansen et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-377 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..244C/abstract): 480,729 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.821 +/- 0.371 solar masses from Christiansen et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-377 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..244C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4200 +/- 138 K from Christiansen et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-377 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..244C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Christiansen et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-377 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..244C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-377.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.673, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
